vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lobstercash
Version: 0.0.2

The 'lobstercash' skill bundle provides high-risk financial capabilities, including sending cryptocurrency, signing arbitrary blockchain transactions, and revealing full virtual credit card details (PAN, CVC, and CVV) directly to the agent's output stream (references/cards.md). While the instructions are clearly aligned with the stated purpose of the Lobster Cash payment service and emphasize human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval, the inherent risk of financial loss and sensitive data leakage—compounded by the use of 'npx' to execute remote code and the ability to make arbitrary network requests via the x402 protocol—meets the threshold for a suspicious classification. There is no evidence of malicious intent, but the primitives provided are highly sensitive and require strict sandboxing.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions align with a payment/wallet purpose, but it directs the agent to install and run an unvetted npm CLI (npx/@crossmint/lobster-cli) and permits signing/executing arbitrary serialized transactions from external sources with inconsistent human-approval requirements — these are disproportionate risks that deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (payment wallet, virtual cards, sending crypto, x402 payments) match the commands and reference docs. The skill does not request unrelated env vars, binaries, or config paths; all instructions revolve around the lobstercash CLI and payment flows, so capabilities are coherent with purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and reference files instruct the agent to run the lobstercash CLI for all flows, to reveal virtual card credentials, to request deposits, and to sign/approve transactions. Most flows require human approval before money is spent, but there are weak spots: the tx/serialized-transaction flow allows signing external serialized transactions supplied by other tools/agents without a clearly enforced human-in-the-loop confirmation in the tx reference. That creates a route for an external system/agent to ask the lobstercash CLI to sign arbitrary on-chain calls. The skill also instructs use of npx to fetch/run the CLI at runtime (remote code execution) which expands the agent's trusted surface beyond local code — this is within-scope for payments but raises operational risk that should be considered.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec included (instruction-only), but the docs explicitly tell the agent to run 'npx @crossmint/lobster-cli' or 'npm install -g @crossmint/lobster-cli'. That means executing remote npm-published code on-demand. The package identity is third-party and not pinned to a specific release/sha in the skill, so runtime installs are not pre-vetted. This is a moderate-to-high operational risk compared with an instruction-only skill that only calls built-in safe tools.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, credentials, or config paths — which is proportionate. However, the runtime actions involve handling sensitive secrets (virtual card numbers, CVC, and signing keys managed by the CLI). The skill claims the CLI stores keys locally and that virtual cards are privacy-preserving, but that trust boundary is external to the skill. Users should verify how the CLI stores credentials and who can access the approval URLs and revealed card data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not 'always:true' and defaults to user-invocable/autonomous invocation allowed (normal). Because it enables financial operations (creating cards, deposits, signing transactions), autonomous invocation combined with the ability to install/run a remote CLI increases attack surface. There is no evidence the skill modifies other skills or system settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says (a payment/wallet assistant) but it has two practical risks you should weigh before installing or enabling it: (1) it tells the agent to run an unpinned npm package via npx/@crossmint/lobster-cli, which fetches and executes remote code at runtime — verify the package's publisher, audit its source, and prefer pinned releases or vendor-reviewed packages; (2) it enables signing/approving on-chain transactions and revealing virtual card credentials. Ensure strict human-in-the-loop policies: require explicit, unambiguous user confirmation before any spend, block automatic approvals, and restrict autonomous invocation for this skill if possible. Also verify where the CLI stores keys and card data (local encrypted store vs remote). If you cannot audit the npm CLI or enforce confirmation and invocation limits, treat this skill with caution or avoid installing it.
llm.findings: [regex-scan-none] expected: No code files were present for the static scanner to analyze; the skill is instruction-only so the scanner found nothing. This absence of findings is expected but not evidence of safety because the runtime will execute an external npm CLI.
